title: Alleged Abuse of Power on 38 Oxley Road
what_it_is: Alleged Abuse of Power on 38 Oxley Road

sections.label: Allegations on Oxley Road and nepotism
sections.summary: The passage lists three matters: the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road, the Deed of Gift for artefacts, and nepotism accusations, which it calls baseless but damaging.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: One, the setting up of the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road; two, the Deed of Gift for some artefacts from the house that were to be displayed in an exhibition by the National Heritage Board; and three, accusations of nepotism over my wife and son, and accusations that I want my father's house kept standing to bolster my power.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: These allegations are entirely baseless but they have already damaged Singapore's reputation.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Unrebutted, they can affect Singaporeans' confidence in the Government.

sections.label: Prime Minister apologises to Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Prime Minister says he deeply regrets that this has happened and apologises to Singaporeans for it.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: As your Prime Minister, I deeply regret that this has happened and apologise to Singaporeans for this.

sections.label: Statement outside the House
sections.summary: He stands by what he will say in the Chamber and will separately issue it as a statement outside the House, not covered by Parliamentary privilege.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I stand by what I will say in this Chamber.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I shall be separately issuing whatever I say in this debate as a statement by me outside the House which will not be covered by Parliamentary privilege.

sections.label: Father's wish to demolish house
sections.summary: His father's long-held wish, known to all Singaporeans, was for the house at 38 Oxley Road to be demolished.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: My father's wish, held for many years, is well-known to all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: He wanted the house at 38 Oxley Road to be demolished.

sections.label: House has no architectural merit
sections.summary: The passage says the house is not worth restoring and has no merit as architecture, and asks that his wish to demolish it be respected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: It is not worth the restoration, unless they restore it just for people to look at. 38 Oxley Road has no merit as architecture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, please respect my wish to have it demolished when I am no longer around." Cabinet noted his letter.

sections.label: Ministers opposed demolishing the house
sections.summary: He thought meeting the Ministers would let his father convince Cabinet, but the Ministers were unanimous in opposing demolition, and he expressed no view as he was conflicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I thought that with his force of personality and conviction, meeting the Ministers would give him the best chance to convince Cabinet, as he had done so many times before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But the Ministers were unanimous in expressing their opposition to knocking the house down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I was the only one who did not express a view, because I was both a son and the Prime Minister and, therefore, conflicted.

sections.label: Father's choice on 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: Father chose to demolish and redevelop the house and donate proceeds to charity, and in August 2011 willed 38 Oxley Road to the speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: At one point, my brother suggested that my father gift the property to Singapore, subject to the condition that the house be demolished and a small public park be built in its place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I said that I thought this was worth considering, but I offered another option: to demolish the house and redevelop the site as my father wanted, but then to sell off the property and donate the proceeds to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I asked my father between the two which he preferred, and he replied the latter, in other words, demolish the house, redevelop and sell off, and donate the proceeds to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: In August 2011, about a month after the Cabinet meeting, my father decided to will 38 Oxley Road to me as part of my share of his estate, and he told the family so.

sections.label: Father's December 2011 instructions
sections.summary: In December 2011 the father told the family it was best to redevelop 38 Oxley Road straightaway after his death, and wrote to Cabinet a third time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: In December 2011, he told the family that it was "best to redevelop 38 Oxley Road straightaway" after he died and do what we proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: At around the same time, on 27 December 2011, he wrote to Cabinet a third time.

sections.label: Architect's authorisation and URA approval
sections.summary: The father signed a letter on 28 March 2012 authorising an architect to submit a development application for 38 Oxley Road, which URA approved on 17 April 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, Members will see, the first page, is my father's authorisation letter to the architect to submit the development application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: He signed it on 28 March 2012: "I hereby authorise you to act as my agent to submit on my behalf an application to the competent authority under the Planning Act 1998 for a written permission to develop lot 99909X TS20" − that means Town Sub-division 20 − "at 38 Oxley Road for proposed additions and alterations to existing two-storey detached dwelling house, River Valley Planning Area." And so on. "I hereby authorise you to pay on my behalf to the competent authority all processing fees or charges payable by me in connection with the application." The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) approved it a few weeks later on 17 April 2012.

sections.label: Father's will and demolition clause
sections.summary: The father died on 23 March 2015; his will, read on 12 April 2015, gave 38 Oxley Road to the speaker and contained a demolition clause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: My father passed away on 23 March 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: On 12 April 2015, three weeks later, his last will was formally read to me and my two siblings. 38 Oxley Road was given to me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The demolition clause was in two main parts with a third minor part at the end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I will read it out in full: "I further declare that it is my wish and the wish of my late Wife, KWA GEOK CHOO, that our house at 38 Oxley Road, Singapore 238629 ("The house") be demolished immediately after my death, or if my daughter Wei Ling, would prefer to continue living in the original house, immediately after she moves out of the house.

sections.label: Wei Ling staying in the house
sections.summary: The father's will expressed his wish that Wei Ling be allowed to stay in the house as long as she wished, so the Government would decide nothing until she no longer stayed there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And in his will, my father had expressed his wish that Wei Ling be allowed to stay there for as long as she wished.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, I said we should honour that, and that I would say in Parliament the next day that the Government would not make any decision, until such time as my sister was no longer staying there.

sections.label: Recusal from 38 Oxley Road decisions
sections.summary: The speaker recused himself from all Government decisions on 38 Oxley Road and placed Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean in charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: One, I recused myself from all Government decisions relating to 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I was conflicted, being my father's son, the inheritor of the house and also the Head of the Government, it was not proper for me to take part in any decisions on 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, at the next Cabinet meeting, two days after the Parliament Sitting, I recused myself from all discussions and decisions relating to the house, and placed Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean in charge.

sections.label: Transferring house to sister
sections.summary: He offered to transfer the house to his sister for $1, with sale or acquisition proceeds going to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I was not sure why, but I thought the best way to resolve the matter was to transfer the house to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I first offered to transfer the house to my sister for a nominal sum of $1, on condition that if the property is sold later or acquired by the Government, all proceeds or compensation would go to charity.

sections.label: Family not benefiting from house
sections.summary: The arrangement addressed his concern that the family not benefit financially from 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, I give one times the value, he gives away one-half times the value, the house is with him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: That complicated arrangement substantially addressed a major concern of mine: that was, that our family be seen not to be benefiting financially from 38 Oxley Road, either through receiving compensation from the state for acquisition or resisting acquisition or preservation/conservation to profit by redeveloping and selling the property.

sections.label: Father's wish to demolish house
sections.summary: He says all want the father's wish to knock the house down, and he has no interest in it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: We all want our father's personal wish to be carried out, which is to knock the house down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I no longer have any interest in the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I do not take part in any Government decisions on the house.

sections.label: Committee lists options only
sections.summary: The Government stated the Committee will only list options and make no decisions on the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: In any case, the Government has stated that the Committee will not make any decisions on the house and will not even recommend any decisions on the house to Cabinet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: The Committee will only list options for the house, so that when a decision does become necessary one day, perhaps decades from now, the Cabinet of the day, most likely by then under a different Prime Minister, will have these options available to consider.

sections.label: Deputy, colleague or Cabinet
sections.summary: He says the decision could be made by a deputy, senior colleague or the rest of the Cabinet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: It could be his deputy, it could be some other senior colleague, it could be the rest of the Cabinet, as in this case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: This is exactly what I have done in the case of 38 Oxley Road.

sections.label: Deputy Prime Minister Teo in charge
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Teo is in full charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo is in full charge.

sections.label: Oxley Road artefacts gifted to NHB
sections.summary: After his father died, the speaker's siblings gifted 38 Oxley Road artefacts to the National Heritage Board, formalised in a Deed of Gift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: After my father passed away, my siblings gifted artefacts from 38 Oxley Road to the National Heritage Board (NHB).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: This was formalised in a Deed of Gift.

sections.label: Concern over Deed terms
sections.summary: After reading the Deed, the speaker became very concerned over what the NHB had agreed to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: After reading the Deed, I became very concerned over what the NHB had agreed to.

sections.label: Conditions in Deed fine print
sections.summary: The siblings publicly announced a gift, but set conditions in the fine print allowing them to take back all items for $1 if terms were breached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Furthermore, my siblings had announced publicly that this was a gift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But, in fact, they had set conditions in the fine print: if at any time, if any of the terms of the Deed were breached, my siblings could immediately take back all the items for $1.

sections.label: Allegations against character and Government
sections.summary: The siblings made allegations against the speaker's character and damaged the Government's reputation, affecting people's trust in the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: My siblings have made allegations against my character and damaged the Government's reputation, affecting people's trust in the Government.

sections.label: Prime Minister recused from house decisions
sections.summary: As Prime Minister, the speaker recused himself from all Government decisions relating to the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: As Prime Minister, I have recused myself from all Government's decisions relating to the house.

sections.label: House transferred and value donated
sections.summary: To pacify them, the speaker offered to transfer the house to his sister for $1, later sold it to his brother, and donated the full value to charity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: To pacify them, I offered to transfer the house to my sister at a nominal sum of $1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Later, I sold the house to my brother, and I donated the full value of the house to charity.

sections.label: PM clarifying allegations in Parliament
sections.summary: The Prime Minister says he cannot leave the matter alone because allegations affected trust in the Government and Singapore's standing, so he must clarify it in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: But as the Prime Minister, I am very clear that I cannot leave this matter alone because the allegations have affected the people's trust in the Government and Singapore's standing in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I must clarify this matter in Parliament, set the record straight, and show that my team and I are determined to defend the Government's integrity and the rule of law.

sections.label: Ministers answering questions, Whip lifted
sections.summary: The Prime Minister says he and his Ministers will answer all questions comprehensively because they have nothing to hide, and he has lifted the Party Whip for PAP MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: My Ministers and I will deal with all their questions and give comprehensive answers because we have nothing to hide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: I have told the People's Action Party (PAP) MPs that I am lifting the Party Whip.

sections.label: MPs should query vigorously
sections.summary: All MPs, including PAP, Opposition and Nominated MPs, should query the Prime Minister and his Ministers vigorously and without restraint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: All MPs, whether PAP MPs, Opposition MPs or Nominated MPs (NMPs), should query me and my Ministers vigorously and without restraint.

sections.label: Ministerial conduct and Rules of Prudence
sections.summary: Ministers are bound by a code of conduct tabled in Parliament, and the Prime Minister issues Rules of Prudence to PAP MPs after every General Election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: Ministers are bound by a code of conduct which is tabled in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And after every General Election, I issue Rules of Prudence to every PAP MP, so that they know how to conduct themselves to protect their own reputation and to safeguard the integrity of the PAP Government and the Singapore system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: When the dust has settled on this unhappy episode, people must know that the Government in Singapore operates transparently, impartially and properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: That in Singapore, even Mr Lee's house and Mr Lee's wishes are subject to the rule of law.
